statement: For every integer d ≥ 2 and every χ > 0 there is a number δ(d, χ) > 0 for which the following data do not exist: 1. a smooth oriented d-manifold Y without boundary, possibly disconnected, with a torus- stabilized metric G satisfying ScalG ≥ χ; 32 2. a smooth map F : Y → Sd, equal to one value outside a compact set, such that deg F ̸= 0 and ∥dF∥op ≤ δ(d, χ) everywhere. The constant is independent of the finite circle count in Equation (7.1). Neither the base metric nor the stabilized metric is assumed complete.
